grammar.title: Reporting Verbs (suggest, advise, deny, refuse)
grammar.explanation:
Instead of **say** and **tell**, we often use a **reporting verb** that shows the speaker's purpose. *'I'll help you,' he said* becomes *He **offered to help** me.*

Some verbs take **verb + to-infinitive**: **agree**, **offer**, **promise**, **refuse**, **threaten**. *She **refused to answer** when Tomas asked about the broken cable.*

Other verbs take an object: **verb + object + to-infinitive**. Use **advise**, **warn**, **remind**, **encourage** and **persuade** this way: *He **advised me to check** the button on the camcorder.*

The negative infinitive is **not to**: *She **warned me not to touch** the chemical.* Never say *warned me don't touch*.

**Deny**, **admit**, **suggest** and **recommend** take **verb + -ing**, with no to. *He **denied pressing** the button, and Nina **suggested filming** the cell again.*

Some verbs need a preposition: **apologise for + -ing**, **insist on + -ing**, **accuse somebody of + -ing**, **congratulate somebody on + -ing**. *They **accused him of cutting** the cable.*

**Suggest** is special: it never takes object + to-infinitive. Say *Tom **suggested going*** or *Tom **suggested that we go***, never *suggested us to go*.

Many reporting verbs also take a **that clause**: **admit that**, **deny that**, **insist that**, **claim that**. *He **admitted that** the camcorder was his.* If friends **back up** your story, reporting verbs help you retell it exactly.
examples: *My boss **advised me to take** a break.* (advise sb to)
*Mum **reminded me to take** my passport.* (remind sb to)

practice.q: Rewrite as reported speech: 'I will check the cable,' he said. Start: He offered ___
practice.a: He offered to check the cable.

practice.q: Rewrite using warned: 'Don't touch the chemical,' she said to Nina.
practice.a: She warned Nina not to touch the chemical.

practice.q: Rewrite using denied: 'I didn't press the button,' he said.
Rewrite using suggested: 'Let's film the cell with the camcorder,' Nina said.
practice.a: Nina suggested filming the cell with the camcorder.

quiz.question: 'I'll help you with your homework,' Dad said. → Dad offered ___ me with my homework.
'Don't touch the cooker,' she said to her son. → She warned her son ___ the cooker.
'I didn't take the money,' he said. → He denied ___ the money.
'Why don't we go to the beach?' Tom said. → Tom suggested ___ to the beach.
'You should see a doctor,' my friend said. → My friend advised me ___ a doctor.
'I'm sorry I'm late,' she said. → She apologised ___ late.
'You broke the window!' the neighbour said to me. → The neighbour accused me ___ the window.
'Congratulations on passing your exam!' they said. → They congratulated me ___ my exam.
'Remember to buy some bread,' Mum said to me. → Mum reminded me ___ some bread.
'I won't sign the contract,' he said. → He refused ___ the contract.
